newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM aluminium ends higher despite dollar drop.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM aluminium ends higher despite dollar drop.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures on Wednesday finished firmer across the board in thin trade, shrugging off the dollar's renewed fall, traders said.

"People were rattled when they saw the yen rising again," one trader said. "But it was offset by the metal's rise in London overnight, so prices did not move much. People are more concerned about the precious metal market."
The TOCOM benchmark April 1998 contract ended 0.7 yen higher at 189.0 yen per kg, after fluctuating in a narrow 189.6 to 188.4 yen range. The other contracts gained 0.2 to 0.6 yen.
Estimated volume was 1,144 lots, compared with 2,444 lots on Tuesday.
The dollar sank below 111 yen in Tokyo to its lowest level in nearly seven months.

In London overnight, three-month aluminium finished up $14 at $1,617 per tonne, helped by declines in LME warehouse and IPAI producer stocks and signs that the contango may have started to contract again.
